# Dynamic JSON renderer (`lib/src/dynamic/`)

`WDynamic` renders a widget tree from JSON that may come from an untrusted source, so the allowlist and the recursion cap are security properties, not conveniences.

## Allowlist

- `WDynamicConfig.isAllowed(type)` resolves in this order: `config.builders[type]` (always allowed, even when listed in `denyWidgets`), then `denyWidgets`, then `defaultWindWidgets` and `defaultFlutterWidgets`. A custom builder is therefore trusted host code and bypasses the deny list; do not route an untrusted type name to one.
- A new built-in type needs three edits that stay in step: the set in `w_dynamic_config.dart`, a `case` in `_buildByType`, and its `_build<Type>` method. A type in the set without a `case` renders the "No builder" error widget, and a `case` without the set entry is unreachable.
- `maxDepth` (default 50) is the recursion-bomb guard. Keep it enforced on every nested build, and have the caller lower it for a surface a remote source must not reach. `denyWidgets` alone does not block a type registered in `builders` (see above), so the control for such a surface is to leave the type out of `builders` and also deny it.
- JSON is untrusted: `type`, `props` and `children` of the wrong shape must degrade (an `Unknown` type the allowlist rejects, empty props, no children), never throw out of `build()`.

## State and actions

- `WDynamic` listens to `WDynamicState` and rebuilds the whole tree on every write; that listener is what makes an `id`-bound widget re-read its value. Without it a `WCheckbox` writes `true`, keeps rendering unchecked and cannot be unticked, because `WDynamicState.set` drops an unchanged value. `addIdListener` is the host-facing watch behind `WDynamicController.addListener`, not the render path.
- Ownership: `WDynamic` disposes its state only when it built it. A state that arrives through a `controller` belongs to the host, so the listener is removed before the ownership check in `dispose`.
- `parseAction` (for `onTap`) injects nothing. `parseValueAction<T>(prop, stateId:)` (for `onChange`) writes `state.set(stateId, value)` first, then dispatches with the value merged into the args as `_value`.
- `WDatePicker` is the exception: `_buildWDatePicker` uses `parseAction`, so the `DateTime` is read from `state.get(id)` inside the handler, not from `args['_value']`.
- Dispatch ignores an unknown action name (`debugPrint` only) and catches a synchronous handler exception, but an async handler's `Future` error escapes. Actions are injected by the host; never hard-code a handler in the renderer.
- A `WSelect` with plain string options and no `value` renders the red error widget (the inferred `WSelect<String>` rejects a null value; `w_dynamic_renderer_test.dart` pins it). Use map-shaped options (`{'value': 'a', 'label': 'Alpha'}`), which render without a `value`.

## Icons

`_parseIcon` lowercases the name before looking in `config.customIcons`, so a `customIcons` key must be lowercase or it never matches.
